chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the debt comes before the bequest, then the bequest follows the debt, then the inheritance comes after the bequest, for indeed the first judgment is the Book of Allah.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤُمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct order for settling debts, bequests, and inheritance in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Imam al-Sadiq from Imam Ali, establishes the canonical hierarchy of estate distribution: debts (al-dayn) take precedence, followed by bequests (al-wasiyyah), and finally inheritance (al-mirath). This sequence is rooted in the divine command 'After any bequest you bequeath or any debt' (Quran 4:11), ensuring that obligations to creditors and specific beneficiaries are settled before the residual wealth is divided among heirs according to their fixed shares.
